title: Jensen Huang Agrees to Testify Before Congress by Thanksgiving
dek: Ex-Nvidia CEO faces House panels over alleged ties to a suspected Chinese spy.

facts.label: Colette Kress named interim Nvidia CEO

caption:
The man behind the chips powering the AI boom is heading to Capitol Hill. ⚠️

Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has agreed to testify before Congress before Thanksgiving, after lawmakers made it clear a subpoena was on the table. House Foreign Affairs Chairman Brian Mast announced the deal, the same day Huang resigned from Nvidia. The closed-door session will cover his alleged ties to a woman suspected of spying for China.

The request came from three powerful chairmen covering foreign affairs, the China Select Committee and intelligence, a sign Congress sees this as a national security issue, not just a boardroom scandal. CFO Colette Kress is now interim CEO and faces her first earnings call on Tuesday.

Why it matters: nearly every major AI tool runs on Nvidia GPUs, and this inquiry could shape future AI chip export rules for China. We're tracking every twist at AI Parabellum.

post_caption:
A subpoena threat did the trick: Jensen Huang will sit down with House lawmakers behind closed doors before Thanksgiving.

The session, expected to be filmed and transcribed, puts the ex-Nvidia chief's alleged China ties in front of three national security panels while Colette Kress steps in as interim CEO.
